messages.content:
You are generating contextual Say/Do previews for an interactive romance story.

FATE CARD SELECTED:
- Title: Temptation
- Theme: A sudden, overwhelming urge.
- Generic Action: Something here calls to you against your better judgment.
- Generic Dialogue: "Why does this feel so familiar?"

CARD STRATEGY — TEMPTATION (deliciously transgressive impulse the protagonist will pay for later but can't resist NOW):
- A temptation is a SPECIFIC IMPULSE the protagonist has been suppressing — and now acts on. It MUST carry tangible risk (social, romantic, legal, dignified, professional) and a guilty-pleasure shimmer. Pick the AXIS that fits the prior beat:
  • EROTIC/PHYSICAL: close distance, initiate touch, cross a sexual threshold, pinch a buttock, run a hand somewhere it shouldn't go, lean in to whisper too close to a mouth, pull at a tie/collar/hem, claim a kiss that wasn't offered. Action is forward physical motion she'll have to explain.
  • SOCIAL TRANSGRESSION (mischief axis — strong on Wry tones): embarrass a haughty official mid-sentence, mimic a pompous accent loud enough to be heard, expose a small hypocrisy in front of witnesses, drop a "compliment" that lands as a cut, spike a stuffy moment with a too-honest aside, neg the deserving, pull a rug out from under someone who had it coming.
  • PETTY CRIME / TAKING (the shiny-thing axis): pocket something not hers (a token, a trinket, a champagne flute, a card, a key, a cufflink), tip-and-run, eat the last bite that wasn't hers, sign someone else's name on the bar tab as a joke, leave with the umbrella.
  • RUDENESS TO THE DESERVING: dismiss a sycophant mid-fawn, refuse to thank someone who didn't earn it, walk past the velvet rope, interrupt the windbag, give a server an extra-large tip in front of the tightwad host, eat off the off-limits plate.
  • SELF-SABOTAGING FUN: blow the deadline to do the more interesting thing, accept the dare, pick the wrong door on purpose, follow the stranger one street further than wise.
- The dialogue can be voiced desire, a half-laughed admission, a "did I just say that?" aside, an under-the-breath crack, OR an unrepentant "yes, and I'd do it again." Never hedged, never sanitized.
- The DELICIOUSLY-REGRETTABLE TEST: would the protagonist replay this moment tomorrow with a private grin AND a small wince? If neither — if it's safe AND boring — REWRITE.
- FORBIDDEN for this card (these are NOT temptations, they're availability or polite escalation):
  • "I want this." / "I'm drawn to you." / "Maybe just this once." — confessions of feeling without an action that actually crosses a line. Pair feeling with the SPECIFIC act that crosses the line.
  • "I lean closer." / "I step in." / "I touch the [neutral object]." — pure proximity moves with no transgressive payload.
  • Stepping back, holding ground, drawing a line, asking for space, refusing, pausing, stating limits — these belong to BOUNDARY.
  • Reasoned consent ("Are you sure?", "We should think about this") — temptation is the OPPOSITE of pause-to-think.
- TONE-AWARE: if the scene's tone is Wry/Comedic, lean into mischief axes (social transgression / petty crime / rudeness to the deserving) — let the temptation be FUNNY first, hot second. If the tone is Earnest/Dark, lean erotic/physical or self-sabotaging.
- ── AXIS CLARITY (HARD — 2026-05-22) ──
  Temptation is a RELATIONSHIP-FORWARD card (when the LI is on stage): the impulse pursued is toward HIM, toward INTIMACY, toward CONNECTION the protagonist has been suppressing. Even when the temptation is mischief-coded (social transgression), the SAY/DO should make the LI a witness, target, or co-conspirator so the choice reads as "I am leaning into him" rather than "I am acting alone."
  REQUIRED FORM: temptation that engages with the LI. Examples that PASS (LI is named/implicated; a fresh seeded subset shows each time the card fires — do NOT copy wording):
    • "Forget the meeting. Let me kiss you here, where they can see." (erotic + uses LI as target)
    • "Come closer. I want to know what you smell like." (sensory + LI as object of desire)
    • "Watch this." (then mocks the pompous CEO across the room) — mischief but LI is invited into the conspiracy
    • "If you can keep up." (challenge + dare to LI, intimate-coded)
  Examples that FAIL (axis-ambiguous solo mischief, no LI engagement):
    • "Watch me leave with the umbrella." — petty crime alone, LI not part of the moment
    • "Just one more drink." — impulse without LI in the sentence
    • "Why not." — bare consent to whatever, no relational pull voiced
  If the scene has NO LI on stage (early-scene PC-alone moments), Temptation's axis read is weaker — but the card click still registers as a relationship-leaning preference signal (the player WANTS romance content). Output can be solo-mischief in that case; the signal is the click intent, not the rendered line.

CURRENT SCENE CONTEXT:
ng from each end like a question asked twice — and set it in my hands, and closed my fingers around it with his, the scarred wrist against my palm for one deliberate second. “Hold it. I am going to ask you questions, here, in front of them. If you are misaligned when you answer, everyone present will know.” It lay still between my hands. My mouth was uncovered now. I found I still could not speak.

SCENE END-STATE ANCHOR (HARD — READ THE FINAL LINES FIRST): the LAST sentences of the scene above are the AUTHORITATIVE PRESENT MOMENT. Whatever the protagonist just DID at the end overrides the scene's opening premise. If she just QUIT, walked out, abandoned the task, decided, or broke something off, she is NO LONGER doing the thing the scene started with — do NOT generate options that assume she is still mid-task ("finish the report," "get back to the deadline," "smooth it over with the boss"). Every card must proceed from her situation, location, and stance AS OF THE FINAL LINE — her NEXT move from where she now stands, not a continuation of a premise she just abandoned.


EMBODIED TEXTURE (fate cards — OCCASIONAL, compressed, NOT every card):
  When it makes a card LAND harder, fold ONE concrete detail of THIS world into the ≤12-word action — an object / garment / surface, OR (in worlds with non-human bodies or augments) a species-anatomy / augment / lore detail — named exactly, in the world's register, MARKED by the act: "Slam the Patek down between us." / "Grind his card into the marble." / "Crush the orchid in my fist."
  WORLD EMBODIED REGISTER (Fantasy · billionaire opulence): the materials of extreme wealth — unlabelled bespoke cloth, gold-enamel, hand-cut crystal, vicuña, calfskin, cold-pressed glass, marble — rendered specifically, never as "luxury" and (for the principal) never via a recognizable logo
  RULES: NOT every card (clutters + repeats) — the action-forward cards benefit most; drop it on purely verbal / internal beats, when the bare act is sharper, or when it would bloat the line. The detail MUST belong to THIS world/register (e.g. Glass House = contemporary modern, no sci-fi vocab; Fatelands = veilwood / spiralgrass / species anatomy; period worlds = period-true objects). Specific-and-marked > generic-and-decorative.


SCENE PRESENCE: The love interest IS present in this scene, but address the ACTIVE INTERLOCUTOR (below) — reference the love interest (him) romantically ONLY if they are the one the protagonist is being pushed to answer.

PROSE REALITY CHECK (HARD): Use ONLY people, objects, and surfaces that actually appear in the RECENT SCENE TEXT. Do NOT invent props (a table, chair, desk, etc.) the scene has not established. Match the real setting and who is actually present.

DECK EXCLUSION (HARD): NEVER reference the protagonist's tarot deck, the cards, the Marseille deck, or "let the cards decide / draw a card" in ANY action or dialogue — even though the deck appears in the scene. Drawing a card is a SEPARATE player mechanic, NOT a Say/Do option; keep the deck entirely out of the suggestion (no "push the deck aside," no "I'm deciding this, not the cards").

PHYSICAL PRESENCE vs MENTION (HARD — read the scene ENDING): a character being NAMED or referenced is NOT proof they are physically present. References to an ABSENT figure — "his shadow loomed," "Roman Tusk's influence," "she thought of him," "dancing to his tune" — mean that person is NOT in the room. Judge who is present by the scene's STAGING at its END. If the scene ENDS with the protagonist ALONE (they walked away, left, are moving / en route, or no other character shares the immediate space), the cards MUST be about the protagonist's OWN next move, inner stance, or situation. Do NOT suggest blocking, confronting, stepping toward, or addressing a character who is not physically in the scene at that moment ("step into his path" / "meet his eyes" when he is elsewhere is INVALID).

ACTIVE INTERLOCUTOR (HARD — who the cards address): Read the END of the scene text above. The closing beat is pushing the protagonist to RESPOND to someone. The cards must focus on THAT person — whoever just challenged, questioned, accused, or addressed the protagonist — NOT automatically the love interest. This is often an adversary, rival, colleague, or third party, and it can be them EVEN WHEN the love interest is also present in the scene. Use romantic / relationship framing ONLY if the love interest is the person the protagonist is being pushed to answer right now; otherwise match the register to that interlocutor (confrontation, negotiation, deflection, refusal — not romance).


SCENE & PLOT CONTEXT (the "Active scene entities" line is RANKED BY SALIENCE — when referencing a named character/threat/location, prefer the highest-salience entity matching the moment; ignore low-salience entities unless this card's strategy specifically calls for them):

The Dohkar’s Weave-Script went a hard, flat colour that said, whether he liked it or not, that he had noticed who they deferred to. “I can hear where she is aligned,” Julian said, to all of them and to me. “Everything in her points one way. She believes she did not do this.” He did not say what had been done, or by whom. He drew out The Answer — the double-ended shaft, a deep hooked blade curling from each end like a question asked twice — and set it in my hands, and closed my fingers around it with his, the scarred wrist against my palm for one deliberate second. “Hold it. I am going to ask you questions, here, in front of them. If you are misaligned when you answer, everyone present will know.” It lay still between my hands. My mouth was uncovered now. I found I still could not speak.

STORY PARAMETERS:
- Tone: Earnest
- World: Fantasy
- Protagonist: Female
- Love Interest behavioral profile: The Spellbinder commands attention through presence alone. Charm is currency, and {LI_SUBJ} spends it selectively — never by accident. Three moves ahead, {LI_SUBJ} makes surrender feel like your idea.
- Love Interest: Male (use he/him pronouns IF the LI is on stage — see SCENE PRESENCE block above)
- Characters present in current scene: protagonist, love interest

PRONOUN RULE: Use correct pronouns for characters who are CURRENTLY ON STAGE. Do not use LI pronouns when the LI is not in the scene. Never use archetype labels (Storybeau, Storybelle, Storyboo) or archetype titles in any output.

TASK: Generate TWO short, contextual previews that fit THIS EXACT SCENE, obeying the CARD STRATEGY above:
1. "Do" — A specific physical action the protagonist could take RIGHT NOW (max 12 words)
2. "Say" — A specific line of dialogue the protagonist could speak RIGHT NOW (max 15 words, in quotes)

OPPOSITION RULE (CRITICAL): Temptation and Boundary are diametrically opposed choices in the player's hand. If this card is TEMPTATION, the action MUST differ in direction from what a BOUNDARY card would produce in the same scene (and vice versa). Two cards returning the same "step closer" suggestion invalidates the choice — the player cannot tell the cards apart.

These must:
- Reference actual details from the scene (location, objects, other characters)
- Match the Earnest tone
- Feel like natural continuations of what's happening
- Be more specific than the generic card suggestions
- Honor the CARD STRATEGY direction absolutely — ignore any scene momentum that would pull you toward the opposite card

Respond in this EXACT format (no labels, just two lines):
[action on first line]
[dialogue in quotes on second line]
